problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -4 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix above has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=1,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-3.$ Find a Jordan canonical form of the matrix.
worked_solution:
Notice that we are given a $3\times 3$ matrix that has precisely $3$ distinct eigenvalues. 

Therefore, $A$ is diagonalizable, and its Jordan canonical form is

$$
{J}_{1}(2)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(1)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(-3)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

**Note:** The Jordan canonical form is unique up to the order of the Jordan blocks.
